gap: The pane is louder than it needs to be. The snippet and date grey is #8C8C8C (140) against A's #999999 (153), and the hairline is #DFDFDF against #E7E7E7. The two lines of preview under each name compete with the name instead of falling back. The header 'library' is also a bare lowercase folder name with no chevron, where A has 'Library ⌄'. Nothing on it says you can switch Locations from there.
gapTheirs: The pane's paper is #FDFDFD while the page beside it is #F9F9F9. The sidebar reads as a separate, whiter sheet stuck onto the page, not the theme's paper running under both. The only thing keeping the two apart is a faint #E7E7E7 hairline at x=735.
verdict: Both panes share the same 368 px column, the same controls in the same order and nearly the same row height (~155 vs ~150 device px), so the choice comes down to tone. B's darker snippets, heavier hairline and an unlabelled lowercase 'library' make the list feel like a raw directory listing that talks over the manuscript. A keeps the previews quieter and gives the header a visible way to switch, but its whiter pane sits beside the page like pasted-on paper. It's a narrow win for A, and neither pane looks like somewhere I'd keep three years of chapters without checking the folder myself.

Both have a 3 px-ish cyan selection bar at x≈8. On both it sits flush left and isn't inset to line up with the row's icon column.

states.gap: The Location header has lost its menu arrow. A draws 'Library ⌄' with a chevron at about x=245 device px, which tells you it opens a picker; B's 'library' is a bare label with nothing after it, so nothing on screen says you can switch or add a folder there. B's labels in the sort, count and date row are also darker (#8C8C8C against A's #999999), which puts the chrome closer to the snippet text.
states.gapTheirs: The pane is not on the page's paper. The sidebar fills with #FDFDFD while the editor sits on #F9F9F9, so the library is a whiter slab bolted onto a grey page, and the 2px hairline (#E7E7E7) has to sit between two different fields. B's pane and page are both #F7F7F7, so its #DFDFDF hairline is the only thing dividing them.
states.verdict: A's library looks like a separate, brighter panel pasted next to the manuscript. The white-on-grey seam draws the eye away from the page every time you glance left. B puts the file list on the same paper as the page, so it reads as the manuscript's own margin, and its snippets carry more of each document before the ellipsis. B has quietly dropped the arrow that tells you the library header can be opened, and a writer looking for their other folder will click a dead-looking word.
secondary: Selected-row tint is 5 levels below the pane in both: A #F8F8F8 on #FDFDFD, B #F2F2F2 on #F7F7F7

In A the date and name sit at nearly the same baseline; in B the date sits about 3px higher than the name
Footer: A 'In this browser', B 'On this device'; same dot and 'All changes saved' in both, B's text slightly darker
Both show '2 of 8 documents' with the query 'sea' highlighted in #B8E6F8-ish chips; search state not judged
